request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIRS:
PAIR 1:
A: TopicEmbed.import assigns the topic's category solely from the embed URL's host record with no fallback (line 42: `category: eh.try(:category_id)`), whereas the removed embed_category setting applied to every import. Any import path not preceded by a host check — feed-polling imports being the notable one — silently lands in Uncategorized instead of the previously configured category.
B: TopicEmbed.import now derives the post's category solely from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) (eh.try(:category_id)), so an import whose URL matches no whitelisted host posts to Uncategorized, while the migration deletes the embed_category setting that previously routed such imports. Admins who use the retained feed_polling_* features with a feed URL whose host is not an embeddable host — or with no hosts configured at all — find every newly imported RSS/ATOM topic in Uncategorized after the upgrade, with the setting that used to control this destroyed and no replacement anywhere in the new UI.

PAIR 10:
A: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host edge cases untested: hosts saved with ports (allowed by validation regex) never match referers with ports, and lower(host) comparison vs referer casing is not covered; port variants from the old SiteSetting spec were dropped
B: Weakened embed_controller_spec 'missing host' test passes for the wrong reason: it fabricates no host but also doesn't stub a referer, so it fails via the nil-referer path instead of the no-hosts path and can't distinguish the two conditions

PAIR 11:
A: The validation regex explicitly accepts port-bearing entries ((:[0-9]{1,5})?) but record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(...).host, which never contains a port, so a host saved with a port is an allowlist entry that can never match any referer. An admin who enters an origin on a non-standard port (e.g. blog.example.com:8080) gets a successful save, then every embed request from that origin is rejected with Discourse::InvalidAccess — the comment section embedded on that site breaks with no configuration-time warning because the entry validates but is dead on arrival.
B: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host ignores ports/schemes asymmetrically: lookup normalizes via URI(host).host but validation permits port suffixes, so port-specific embed rules silently can't work

PAIR 12:
A: EmbeddingSerializer embeds only embeddable_hosts ids (embed: :ids) without side-loading the objects, causing either N+1 per-host network requests from the client store or unresolved/null rows in the embedding admin page; fix by using embed: :objects
B: EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids, emitting only embeddable_host_ids without inline host objects, likely causing the admin UI template to render blank host/category data and possibly disabling save

PAIR 13:
A: `EmbeddingSerializer#id` serializes an OpenStruct wrapping an AR relation; `has_many :embeddable_hosts` on an OpenStruct is fragile and relies on the relation materializing once
B: OpenStruct used as the 'embedding' model in Admin::EmbeddingController and serialized through EmbeddingSerializer's has_many association; OpenStruct responds to arbitrary methods so serializer contract violations fail silently with nil instead of raising — use an explicit read-only model/presenter struct

PAIR 14:
A: save()'s only in-flight guard is cantSave's host.isSaving — a property Discourse's custom RestModel never defines — so nothing actually prevents concurrent invocations of save(). Pressing Enter in the host input and then clicking the check button (or double-clicking) issues two POSTs before either resolves; the server has no uniqueness validation on EmbeddableHost.host, so both succeed and two identical rows are silently created, visible only after the next page load.
B: host.isSaving may not exist on RestModel: if RestModel (unlike Ember Data) does not define isSaving, the cantSave guard and the disabled=host.isSaving bindings are permanently falsy, and a double-click during a slow save issues two POSTs, creating duplicate host rows.

PAIR 15:
A: The migration joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but the removed embed_category setting stored a category ID string, not a category name, so the join can never match. For every existing production install the category lookup returns empty, category_id resolves to 0 and falls back to the uncategorized category, silently reassigning all embedded-topic routing that previously used embed_category; the advertised data migration never migrates the category.
B: Migration join assumes embed_category stored a category name; if it stored a category id, every migrated host silently falls back to uncategorized
